originality.rationale: Tian’s complete primary Theorem 2.1 gives n for arbitrary disk maps and min(n,d) for inner finite Blaschke maps. It does not state the combined strict-target-radius and arbitrary finite-valence, nonproper optimal constant. Badea–Renard’s primary work studies hyperbolic divided differences and other operators, not this exact Bergman matrix class. Components (area formula, nonnegative kernel coefficients) are classical, but their sharp three-parameter classification and interior collapsing-fiber witness were not found covered.
residual_risks: An existing weighted-composition/area-formula theorem might have explicitly combined these three parameters; finite-point inequality is recent and possible follow-up revisions were not fully searched.
The construction uses classical inequalities, so novelty is the exact combined class threshold and witness, not the elementary components.

value.rationale: The full optimum C_{n,m}(rho) gives a natural quantitative tradeoff between sample number, analytic multiplicity and image contraction and sharpens finite-point Schwarz-Pick in an explicit broad nonproper class. Interior branch-point concentration for rho<1 establishes nontrivial sharpness not implied by the three one-sided inequalities alone. No claim of a fixed-map optimum or arbitrary target domains.

limitations: Sharp universal class constant, not each individual map/tuple; image disk centered at 0, m finite, rho in (0,1], complex disk only.
